vacuous_or_weak: RestartLimit is vacuous with respect to its mechanism. It reads the restart counter t.rs, the variable it is meant to check, so with the counter frozen it still holds (r3 rl-uncounted). Read independently from epochs, it fails in 9 parts within 16 steps (r3 rl-uncounted-epochs). It should be restated over epochs and fence reasons.

TwoCoordinatorsAct only restates the --ce fence. A violation means an op ran by a stale coordinator, and FENCE_CE refuses every such op before the property is checked, including the session-tool start, which is not a script. plans() also gives a stale coordinator an empty plan.

NoFalseSuspicion is largely assumed. A watcher tick is enabled only after every healthy child has made a call (tickEnabled), so a slow healthy call can never be suspected. Without that assumption the property fails in all 43 parts within 4 steps (r3 no-timeliness).

Slots excludes children that wrote READY but are still alive. The model also has no close or stop-verify step for committed children (contract decision 17), so Slots is weaker than R10. When the slot is held until a close (r3 ready-holds-slot), liveness fails in every part.

AtMostOneCommit: its mechanism (exclusive create of COMMIT) is never exercised. The A-WX state graph is identical to DF (3,659,461 states) because the model's reconcile marks the row committed from the COMMIT record, and the contract has no such branch. Without that branch, WX is load-bearing (RV-WX-ONLY fails in 6 steps). The property also counts an identical re-write as a second commit.
DRAIN and COMMIT_WX are not shown load-bearing at two faults (A-DRAIN and A-WX hold), as the report says.
The loop rule of R5 is dead code. MODE.LOOPS is never entered (faults set only STUCK, LOOPV and DEAD), so the LOOP threshold is never exercised.
model_errors: The report's state counts belong to an earlier base that had FIX_ENDTURN_RECHECK on. The report's DF2-K2-R1 (3,257,396) equals the rerun's DFPLUS-RECHECK exactly, and its X-ENDTURN-RECHECK (3,659,461) equals the rerun's DF2-K2-R1. Every ablation count is 10-13 % lower than the rerun. The verdicts are not affected.
The model's status --reconcile marks a row committed when a COMMIT record exists (model.mjs:188). The contract's reconcile records only starts. This branch masks COMMIT_WX completely.

FENCE_CE also covers the session-tool start (runOp:261 includes OP.T), but that start is a tool call, not a script with --ce. A stale coordinator also obeys R6 by construction (plans:200). Together these hide a double start that needs no fault.
Reconcile reads the session's true existence at the moment of the start. A transcript that appears later is not modelled (r3 transcript-lag: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail in DF within 3 steps).
The READY re-check reads the child's state in the same atomic step as the CAS fence, although the session writes READY.json without the run lock (r3 ready-race).
Endturn starts the watcher and the alarm itself, in one atomic step. In the contract, endturn only checks; the coordinator then starts them with further tool calls, and the turn can die in between.

A-FENCE-CE has an infinite state space. Without the fence, the draining coordinator keeps handing over: its own kills wake it, it re-arms at each wake, and ce goes 1, 2, 3 in the traces, while the owner keeps starting new coordinators. No memory budget can complete this configuration. k=1 does not make it finite, and the one-byte ce would wrap at 256.
Admission and Slots read true process liveness. The contract's 'unknown' class (process list failed, transcript-only evidence) is not modelled.

Tooling, not the model: run-all.mjs and run-resumable.mjs size their pools to availableParallelism-2 workers at 60 % of free memory: 22 workers in the report's run, and 11 x 670 MB in the first review attempt. r3/runjobs.sh used xargs -P 4. These are the loads that came before the stalls. This attempt ran at most two check.mjs at a time through the lane.
fixes_modelled_as_oracles: FIX_ARM_AT_START: oracle. The alarm is armed in the same step as the wake. As a separate tool call (r3 arm-start-can-die), NoDeadlock and AlwaysCanResolve fail with one fault within 2 steps. The contract does not carry this fix.

FIX_READY_ALL, and the design's READY_WINS: oracle. The re-check is atomic with the child's READY, but the session writes READY.json without the lock. With that race allowed (r3 ready-race), ReadyNotDiscarded fails in 43/43 parts within 5 steps. The contract re-checks only for failure reasons.

FIX_PAUSE_DISCOUNT: oracle. The pause fault sets s.pu, and the tick reads it. A one-sided threshold misses short pauses (r3 pause-short: NoFalseSuspicion fails within 6 steps). The contract dropped this fix.

FIX_WATCHER_ACTIONABLE: close to an oracle. The watcher evaluates the planner's predicate on the true global state, so a disagreement between watch.mjs and the planner is not modelled. The contract keeps only the 'events after acked_seq' part, and that combination (RV-CONTRACT2) fails NoDeadlock, AlwaysCanResolve, EventuallyResolves, ReadyNotDiscarded and NoFalseSuspicion.

FIX_ARM_BY_WRITE: only half modelled. In the untimed model it reduces to not killing the alarm. The contract's decision 5 differs: superseded alarms exit 0 and, under KILL_WAKES, wake the coordinator. These exits are not modelled.
FIX_ADMIT_RESERVE: a mechanism, matching lib.slotCount for admitted rows. But it reads true process liveness, and there is no 'unknown' case.

Design mechanisms are also oracles: RECONCILE reads true session existence; FENCE_CE is applied to a tool call and a stale coordinator obeys R6 by construction; the host class reads a flag set by the reset fault instead of comparing boot identifiers.

extra_flaws.title: A stale coordinator can start a second session: the session-tool start has no --ce fence
extra_flaws.detail: After handover.mjs, the old watcher and alarm exit (64 or superseded), and those exits wake the old coordinator. R6's 'stale ce ends the turn' is a rule the session follows; only scripts are fenced. r4 stale-tool-start, with scripts fenced and the tool start unfenced, on DF2-K2-R1: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail in 9 parts within 4 steps with one fault (3 live sessions > N_max=2). r4 stale-tool-start-yield, where turns are not atomic: they fail in all 22 finished parts, including runs with no fault (drain, hand-over, new coordinator admits f0, then both coordinators start f0e1).
extra_flaws.fix: Fence the start at the child, by script. replace start writes a start token (nonce, task, epoch, ce) under the run lock. The session's start hook (guard-hook.mjs) takes wt/<task>-e<e>/session.lock by exclusive create and checks epoch and ce under the lock. A second session, or one with a stale ce, exits at once. Model the start as two steps: the tool call, then the hook.

extra_flaws.title: READY is written outside the run lock, so it races replace's re-check and fence
extra_flaws.detail: The re-check and the CAS fence both run under the run lock, but the session writes staging/READY.json itself (CONTRACT 3.12). A READY that lands between them is fenced: the work is lost and one restart is charged. r3 ready-race: ReadyNotDiscarded fails in 43/43 parts within 5 steps. The contract also skips the re-check for planned hand-overs and memory parking.
extra_flaws.fix: Make READY a CAS against the fence: the child declares READY through a locked script that refuses when the epoch has moved and records ready@e in the row. replace then reads the row, not the file. Extend the re-check to every non-taint reason.

extra_flaws.title: Reconcile's 'a transcript on disk means the start happened' fails when the transcript appears late
extra_flaws.detail: The turn dies after the start and before bind. The transcript has not appeared yet when reconcile runs, so the row stays 'admitted' and the attempt is started again. r3 transcript-lag: Slots and OneSessionPerAttempt fail in 9 parts within 3 steps. The contract only flags several-sessions after the fact.
extra_flaws.fix: Use a two-phase start: record start-requested under the lock before the tool call. Reconcile treats start-requested without a transcript as unknown, never as not started. The folder lock refuses a second session in any case.

extra_flaws.title: The session arms the wake sources, so one dead turn can leave none
extra_flaws.detail: In the contract, endturn only checks; the coordinator then starts watch.mjs and the alarm with its own tool calls. A turn that dies before those calls, or a first turn that dies before any call, leaves no wake source, and R6's bound does not count this case. r3 arm-start-can-die: NoDeadlock fails with one fault within 2 steps. RV-CONTRACT also fails NoDeadlock within 2 steps.
extra_flaws.fix: Count a turn that dies before arming as a lost wake in R6's bound. Add a dead-man check outside the tree (a scheduled task reads watcher.lock and alarm.json freshness and alerts the owner), and state it as the recovery path.

extra_flaws.title: The contract carries two of the six adopted fixes, and that combination fails at two faults
extra_flaws.detail: Modelled as built (RV-CONTRACT-K2 in r3, RV-CONTRACT2 in r4), the contract fails ReadyNotDiscarded (43 parts), NoFalseSuspicion, NoDeadlock (2 steps), AlwaysCanResolve and EventuallyResolves. The report's 'all 14 hold' is for DF, not for what is being built.
extra_flaws.fix: Carry the actionable watcher predicate, the READY re-check for every non-taint reason, and a robust arming path into the contract. Or record these failures as open defects of the build.

extra_flaws.title: Hang counts ticks without a new call, so a healthy slow call is suspected
extra_flaws.detail: One long model or tool call that lasts longer than h x delta looks like a hang. The model removes this case by assumption; without the assumption, NoFalseSuspicion fails in every part within 4 steps (r3 no-timeliness). A false hang costs the one restart that R=1 allows.
extra_flaws.fix: Count hang on no transcript growth (bytes, streamed tokens), not on no new call. Calibrate h against the slowest healthy call in the pilot. Model a slow but healthy child as normal behaviour, not as fault cs.

extra_flaws.title: A committed child keeps its slot until a close that only the session performs
extra_flaws.detail: Under contract decision 17, the slot is freed only after the coordinator closes the session and stop verify confirms. When the slot is held until a close (r3 ready-holds-slot), AlwaysCanResolve and EventuallyResolves fail in every part, within 1 step at N_max=1. The model has no close step.
extra_flaws.fix: Model the close and stop verify. Have the watcher raise an event for a committed attempt whose process is still alive, so a script drives the close.

verdict:
The model reproduces the report's verdicts. The complete rerun is in model-review/r3/out/rerun: 1041 parts, all two-fault configurations, no errors. For DF2-K2-R1, D2-K2-R1 and every A-* and X-* configuration, the same properties fail and hold as in the report. The state counts do not match: the report's base and ablation numbers come from an earlier base with FIX_ENDTURN_RECHECK on, and its DF and DF+RECHECK labels are swapped. A-RESTART-LIMIT and D2-K2-R1-NOKILLWAKE now have complete K2 results that agree with the report's probes. A-FENCE-CE is still memory-bounded at k=1, because its state space is infinite. The files k3-*, k4*, df3k2, big and guard under model-review come from the first review attempt, which was interrupted by the PC reset; they are evidence only. In them, DF2-K3-R1, DF2-K3-R2, DF3-K2-R1 and DF3-K2-R2 are complete with all properties holding, and DF2-K4 is bounded with no failure found.

The search is exact within its bounds. It compares full states, reports memory bounds explicitly, and its reductions (canonical form, atomic turns) change no DF verdict. Each of the ten safety properties fails when a mechanism is broken. But RestartLimit is vacuous with respect to its counter, TwoCoordinatorsAct only restates the fence, and NoFalseSuspicion is largely assumed by the timeliness rule.

Four of the six adopted fixes are modelled as oracles that act atomically on true state: arm at start, the READY re-check, the pause discount and the actionable watcher. So are the design's reconcile and its --ce fence. When those oracles are replaced by what the contract actually has, DF itself fails:
- A stale coordinator starts a second session in an admitted attempt and exceeds N_max. This needs one fault with atomic turns, and no fault when turns are not atomic (r4 stale-tool-start, a new mutant run in this attempt).
- READY races the fence (r3 ready-race).
- A late transcript leads to a double start (r3 transcript-lag).
- One dead turn leaves no wake source (r3 arm-start-can-die).

The model's result that all 14 properties hold applies to an idealised DF. The contract being built carries two of the six fixes, and at two faults it fails liveness and ReadyNotDiscarded.
